speaker: Doctor
text: Given the isolated hypertension in the right arm and the negative review of systems, I am concerned about a vascular anomaly like coarctation or aortic arch obstruction. I will now perform a physical examination to compare pulses and blood pressure in all four limbs and listen for a murmur. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Pressure_All_Extremities.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal. Blood Pressure All Extremities: Upper Extremities 150/80 mm Hg (Right), compared to lower values in lower extremities. Pulses: 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses. Heart Auscultation: Normal S1 and S2, 2/6 long systolic murmur with systolic ejection click over the left sternal border and back. Chest X-ray: Normal heart size, rib notching not observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The echocardiogram confirms a narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a significant gradient, and the physical exam shows weak femoral pulses compared to strong radial pulses. These findings, combined with the blood pressure discrepancy between the upper and lower extremities, are diagnostic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.
